resources.string: Stopped · tap the button below to start
>8m (out of range) — echo beyond reliable phone-speaker range
Measuring — first echo in about 1.5 s
Fires a 60ms linear chirp (3-8kHz) every 1.5 s; distance = echo delay relative to direct sound × 343m/s ÷ 2.
Not enough valid echoes — the curve scrolls in with each valid measurement
Y-axis 0.2-8m; only measurements with a valid echo are plotted. No-echo / out-of-range cycles are not recorded.
[!] Media volume is low — weak speaker output noticeably shortens the range; raise it above 80%
Sound speed is scaled at 343m/s (dry air at 20°C); every 10°C change shifts it by about 6m/s, a ~1.7% distance error.

The speaker and mic are extremely close — direct sound is treated as the 0m time base, so only echoes after it are measured. If system echo cancellation (AEC) erases the direct sound, this page reports \'direct sound not captured\' and never invents a distance.
Multipath reflections, soft surfaces (curtains / sofas / acoustic panels) and oblique angles weaken or kill the echo; large flat targets such as walls, doors and tabletops work best.

Limited by phone speaker power and the 0.5s recording window, the reliable range is about 0.2-8m; beyond 8m it shows \">8m (out of range)\"; in strongly absorbing rooms it shows \"no echo (absorbing room / wrong angle)\".
Bluetooth headsets / external speakers add hundreds of milliseconds of latency and the mic cannot hear the direct sound — use the phone speaker.

Readings are peak-delay estimates, not laser ranging; good for \'is there an obstacle ahead / roughly how far\', not for precision measurement. All readings come from real sampling and local FFT computation; unavailable values show \'--\'.
